question: How does a harsh, fault-finding work culture affect clinical safety?

options.A: It helps supervisors finish their administrative duties much faster
options.B: It forces junior nurses to study their textbooks more frequently
options.C: It encourages staff to report every single minor incident immediately
options.D: It makes nurses hide mistakes out of fear, preventing learning and improvement

explanation: When the environment is too scary, people hide their errors instead of talking about them. True learning happens in safe, open spaces! [learn more](GST321_U1_T17#GST321_U1_T17_h6)

question: Why is it important to keep the head of the bed raised during a home tube feeding?

options.A: To prevent stomach contents from flowing back into the lungs
options.B: To keep the external tubing straight and secure
options.C: To make it easier for the caregiver to reach the pump
options.D: To help the formula digest faster in the stomach

explanation: Spot on! Elevation uses gravity to keep the liquid formula safely in the stomach, preventing dangerous aspiration. [learn more](GNS324_U3_T7#GNS324_U3_T7_h5)

question: Why are cooking demonstrations more effective than simply handing out printed pamphlets?

options.A: They show mothers how to use local foods in practical, hands-on ways
options.B: They eliminate the need for any further nursing follow-up
options.C: They prove that imported foods are always superior
options.D: They take less time than talking to individuals

explanation: Hands-on cooking demos help learners visualize and practice preparing nutritious meals with ingredients they already own. [learn more](GNS227_U3_T003#GNS227_U3_T003_h6)

question: Why should a practical nurse manager care about abstract ideas on human nature?

options.A: They determine whether a manager uses strict control or empowers staff
options.B: They dictate the specific brand of medical supplies the ward purchases
options.C: They help the finance department calculate payroll taxes accurately
options.D: They are required by law to be written in every employee contract

explanation: What you believe about people shapes how you lead them! If you think staff need close watching, you micromanage. If you trust them, you delegate. [learn more](GST321_U1_T1#GST321_U1_T1_h1)

question: What major environmental problem is caused by poorly operated, low-temperature medical incinerators?

options.A: Complete disappearance of municipal electricity grids
options.B: Release of toxic dioxins and furans into the air
options.C: Immediate flooding of nearby hospital wards
options.D: Excessive production of harmless oxygen gas

explanation: Burning medical waste at low temperatures without proper filters releases nasty chemical pollutants like dioxins and furans into our air. High standards matter! [learn more](GST114_U6_T13#GST114_U6_T13_h4)

question: What is the most crucial nursing check right after a neck biopsy or fine-needle aspiration?

options.A: Monitoring for signs of airway obstruction or bleeding
options.B: Checking for sudden spikes in fasting blood glucose
options.C: Testing the patient's 24-hour urine catecholamine levels
options.D: Encouraging immediate heavy physical exercise

explanation: Always protect the airway! Since the procedure is right in the neck near major blood vessels and the trachea, nurses must watch closely for swelling or bleeding. [learn more](GNS222_U2_T4#GNS222_U2_T4_h7)

question: What is the main purpose of a strong focal point on a health education poster?

options.A: To make the poster look like a modern art painting
options.B: To hide the official logo of the sponsoring health organization
options.C: To immediately draw the viewer's attention to the core health topic
options.D: To use up empty white space at the bottom of the page

explanation: A great focal point grabs the eye instantly, making sure people catch the main health message even if they just glance at it quickly. [learn more](GNS124_U5_T6#GNS124_U5_T6_h4)

question: How can data from a patient's wearable device assist the nursing staff?

options.A: By ordering hospital meals based on step counts
options.B: By prescribing medication without a doctor's signature
options.C: By showing early warning signs like an unusual rise in resting heart rate
options.D: By diagnosing complex mental health disorders automatically

explanation: Continuous tracking on wearables can alert nurses to subtle physiological changes before a patient's condition deteriorates severely. [learn more](GNS113_U3_T1#GNS113_U3_T1_h5)

question: What causes extra or missing chromosomes, like in Down syndrome?

options.A: Eating too much sugar over the years
options.B: Rapid multiplication of red blood cells during an infection
options.C: A physical injury to the skin in childhood
options.D: Chromosomes failing to separate properly during cell division

explanation: When chromosomes don't pull apart neatly during cell division, the resulting cells can end up with an extra or missing chromosome. You've got this! [learn more](GNS111_U1_T7#GNS111_U1_T7_h5)

question: A woman who delivered a healthy baby six hours ago starts bleeding heavily, and her uterus feels soft and boggy. What should the nurse do first?

options.A: Wait for two hours to see if the bleeding stops on its own
options.B: Leave the ward to call the senior consultant doctor immediately
options.C: Encourage the mother to stand up and walk around the room
options.D: Massage the uterus gently to stimulate contraction and expel clots

explanation: A soft, boggy uterus after delivery indicates uterine atony, which requires immediate fundal massage to stimulate contraction and reduce bleeding. [learn more](GNS216_U1_T7#GNS216_U1_T7_h4)

question: A patient needs an IV line inserted. Which limb area MUST be avoided?

options.A: A forearm showing faint bruising from a previous blood test
options.B: The cephalic vein area of an adult male patient
options.C: The dorsal surface of the non-dominant hand
options.D: An arm with a surgically created dialysis fistula

explanation: Dialysis access points must be protected from punctures, blood draws, and IV lines to preserve blood flow for kidney failure treatment. [learn more](GNS122_U1_T4#GNS122_U1_T4_h2)

question: Which procedure gives the final, sure diagnosis for uterine cancer?

options.A: Complete blood count
options.B: Urinalysis and culture
options.C: Endometrial biopsy
options.D: Abdominal X-ray

explanation: Spot on! Taking a small tissue sample through a biopsy lets the lab confirm if cancer cells are present. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T23#GNS216_U5_T23_h5)

question: Which of the following is a common operational barrier to implementing clinical standards in resource-limited settings?

options.A: Shortages of essential equipment and supplies
options.B: A complete absence of hospital patients
options.C: Too much free time during morning shifts
options.D: An excess of available nursing personnel on every shift

explanation: Without basic tools like gloves, clean water, or drugs, nurses struggle to follow clinical standards properly. [learn more](GST321_U1_T20#GST321_U1_T20_h6)

question: What is a likely result of poor onboarding and weak orientation programs?

options.A: Greater trust between doctors and nurses
options.B: Lower hospital spending on medical supplies
options.C: Faster completion of daily ward chores
options.D: Higher rates of early resignation among new staff

explanation: When new nurses feel unsupported and overwhelmed, they are much more likely to leave the facility quickly. [learn more](GST321_U1_T11#GST321_U1_T11_h4)

question: How do bureaucratic silos hurt community health networks?

options.A: They eliminate all communication costs between health facilities
options.B: They prevent organizations from sharing data and coordinating their community interventions effectively
options.C: They automatically increase the number of trained midwives in rural areas
options.D: They force government ministries to merge with private pharmaceutical companies

explanation: Spot on! When agencies work in separate bubbles, resources get wasted and important gaps pop up in patient care. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T019#GNS226_U5_T019_h7)

question: Why is it important for nurses to understand a patient's cultural background regarding health?

options.A: Culture completely prevents patients from experiencing chronic pain.
options.B: Culture shapes how clients interpret symptoms and choose where to seek care.
options.C: Culture determines the exact medical dosage a patient's liver can metabolize.
options.D: Culture is the single biological cause of all infectious diseases.

explanation: Great thinking! Culture heavily influences whether someone trusts modern medicine, traditional healing, or a mix of both when they feel sick. [learn more](GNS112_U1_T3#GNS112_U1_T3_h6)

question: If a patient's stapes bone becomes fused and stuck, where does sound transmission get blocked first?

options.A: Equalizing pressure through the Eustachian tube
options.B: Capturing sound waves in the external auricle
options.C: Secreting cerumen inside the ear canal
options.D: Transferring vibrations to the oval window of the internal ear

explanation: Since the stapes normally acts like a piston pushing against the oval window, a stuck bone stops that crucial transfer of energy dead in its tracks. [learn more](GNS211_U4_T2#GNS211_U4_T2_h5)

question: Why are anti-diarrhea drugs sometimes avoided when a patient has an infection causing their diarrhea?

options.A: Diarrhea helps the kidneys filter extra salt from the blood
options.B: Antibiotics are the only approved treatment for any diarrhea
options.C: These medications always cause permanent bowel paralysis instantly
options.D: Stopping stool too fast can trap harmful bacteria inside the body

explanation: Makes sense, right? Diarrhea is actually the body's way of flushing out bad germs. Shutting it down too quickly can trap those toxins inside. [learn more](GNS212_U1_T5#GNS212_U1_T5_h5)

question: Which of these is NOT something a nurse checks for safety during a first home visit?

options.A: Safety and cleanliness of the water supply
options.B: Presence of loose rugs or cluttered walkways
options.C: Condition of electrical wiring and cooking areas
options.D: Availability of high-tech robotic surgery equipment

explanation: Correct! We don't expect high-tech operating theatre equipment in a house. Our focus is purely on everyday home safety hazards. [learn more](GNS324_U1_T5#GNS324_U1_T5_h4)

question: Which of these traditional food practices actually goes hand-in-hand with modern science?

options.A: Combining grains and legumes for complete protein
options.B: Avoiding all liquids during a bout of severe diarrhea
options.C: Giving only sugary water to a newborn infant
options.D: Starving a patient completely to cure a high fever

explanation: Mixing grains and legumes (like rice and beans) is a brilliant traditional practice that supplies all essential amino acids our bodies need! [learn more](GNS227_U2_T017#GNS227_U2_T017_h5)

question: A patient comes in with a swollen ulnar nerve and a numb patch on the arm. What should you suspect?

options.A: High blood pressure
options.B: A normal heat rash
options.C: Low blood levels (anemia)
options.D: Leprosy

explanation: When a nerve is thickened and a skin patch loses its feeling, leprosy should immediately come to mind. Spotting these clues makes you a great nurse! [learn more](GNS214_U1_T6#GNS214_U1_T6_h4)

question: Why do many teenage girls avoid going to health clinics for reproductive health issues?

options.A: Mandatory laws requiring parental permission for checkups
options.B: A complete absence of physical illnesses during teenage years
options.C: Fear of judgment and stigma from staff or community members
options.D: The belief that clinics only treat elderly patients

explanation: Exactly. Fear of being gossiped about or judged stops many young people from getting the medical help they truly need. [learn more](GNS312_U3_T11#GNS312_U3_T11_h3)

question: A nurse manager notices constant bickering among staff over shift rosters and fairness. What is the best proactive step to take?

options.A: Scold the entire nursing team during the next morning meeting
options.B: Create a transparent and fair scheduling policy with staff input
options.C: Ban all nurses from discussing their rosters at work
options.D: Ignore the complaints until someone quits their job

explanation: Involving the team to build a clear, fair scheduling system removes the guesswork and perceived injustice that causes roster fights. [learn more](GST321_U5_T2#GST321_U5_T2_h7)

question: How is a painful muscle abscess caused by an unsterile injection usually managed?

options.A: Apply tight bandages to squeeze the trapped fluid out through the skin
options.B: Massage the lump firmly to help disperse the pus into surrounding tissue
options.C: Assist with surgical incision and drainage while maintaining sterile dressings
options.D: Advise the patient to ignore the lump until it dissolves on its own

explanation: Trapped pus has to come out! An abscess requires sterile incision and drainage, followed by proper wound care and antibiotics to help the patient heal. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T4#GNS122_U3_T4_h7)

question: Why is proper documentation of a referral important for the client's care?

options.A: It proves to the government that the nurse worked extra hours
options.B: It prevents the receiving facility from repeating unnecessary assessments
options.C: It allows the nurse to charge extra administrative fees to the client
options.D: It stops the client from ever returning to the primary health center

explanation: Clear notes on clinical history and vital signs save time and guide the receiving team straight to appropriate management. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T029#GNS226_U6_T029_h5)

question: What happens when pyrantel pamoate affects a roundworm's nerves and muscles?

options.A: Migration to the lungs
options.B: Spastic paralysis of the worm
options.C: Rapid growth and reproduction
options.D: Enhanced nutrient absorption

explanation: You got it! Pyrantel locks the worm's muscles in a tight paralysis so it loses its grip on the gut wall and gets pooped out. [learn more](GNS223_U3_T7#GNS223_U3_T7_h3)

question: Why do your hands and lips take up so much more space on the brain's sensory map than your back or thighs?

options.A: The cerebral cortex processes touch differently in the lower body.
options.B: Skin on the back has thicker layers of subcutaneous fat.
options.C: Signals from the upper limbs travel faster than spinal signals.
options.D: The hands and lips contain a much higher density of sensory receptors.

explanation: Well done! Parts of the body that need super-fine touch discrimination require more brain power, giving them a much bigger spot on the sensory homunculus. [learn more](GNS211_U4_T5#GNS211_U4_T5_h6)

question: Why is keeping a hospital ward calm and clean during mealtime so important?

options.A: It prevents nurses from having to clean bedsheets
options.B: It speeds up the digestion rate in the stomach
options.C: It stops patients from talking to one another
options.D: It encourages better appetite and food consumption

explanation: Spot on! A peaceful, clean, and pleasant dining vibe lowers stress and makes patients actually want to eat their meals. [learn more](GNS227_U2_T002#GNS227_U2_T002_h8)

question: A nurse researcher wants local ward staff to immediately adopt a new fall-prevention protocol. Which dissemination channel is most effective?

options.A: Publishing a brief note on a personal entertainment blog
options.B: Holding a hands-on clinical workshop and ward training session
options.C: Mailing hard copies of the raw data tables to the health minister
options.D: Submitting a lengthy letter to an international history journal

explanation: Hands-on workshops give frontline staff direct training and practice with new clinical protocols. [learn more](GNS224_U4_T2#GNS224_U4_T2_h4)

question: How does SIMV (Synchronized Intermittent Mandatory Ventilation) differ from Assist-Control mode?

options.A: SIMV delivers breaths only when the patient makes zero respiratory effort
options.B: SIMV allows spontaneous breaths between mandatory machine breaths without extra volume support
options.C: SIMV is only used for patients who are paralyzed or heavily sedated
options.D: SIMV completely controls every single breath the patient takes without exception

explanation: SIMV gives the patient a bit of freedom! The machine gives scheduled breaths, but in between those, the patient can take their own natural breaths without the machine forcing extra air. [learn more](GNS315_U3_T6#GNS315_U3_T6_h2)

question: Which group of patients is most at risk from drug-resistant infections?

options.A: Individuals living in high-altitude mountain regions
options.B: Young adult athletes with minor sports injuries
options.C: Healthy adults with strong nutritional status
options.D: Immunocompromised patients and neonates

explanation: Exactly right. Newborns and patients with weak immune systems don't have enough backup to fight off tough, resistant bugs when standard medicines fail. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T92#GNS214_U1_T92_h5)

question: Which leadership style is best when a sudden cholera outbreak needs immediate, fast action?

options.A: Autocratic
options.B: Laissez-Faire
options.C: Transformational
options.D: Democratic

explanation: During a rapid emergency like an outbreak, taking charge with clear, direct instructions saves precious time and lives. You're mastering clinical decision-making! [learn more](GNS124_U2_T2#GNS124_U2_T2_h2)

question: Why do researchers use the exact same questions and words for everyone taking a survey?

options.A: It prevents participants from feeling confused by long medical terms
options.B: It guarantees that every participant will finish the survey faster
options.C: It allows the nurse researcher to change the topic mid-interview
options.D: It ensures all answers can be fairly compared across the group

explanation: Using identical wording means any differences in the responses are due to actual differences between people, not because a question was asked differently. Keep pushing forward! [learn more](GNS224_U1_T22#GNS224_U1_T22_h1)

question: A community health nurse notices that traditional birth attendants in a local village reuse unsterilized razor blades. What is the most appropriate intervention?

options.A: Provide education on safe cutting practices and supply proper sterile instruments
options.B: Report the village to the police for practicing illegal medicine
options.C: Ignore the practice since it is part of local cultural heritage
options.D: Refuse to visit the village until the elders sign a formal apology

explanation: Respectful education paired with accessible tools helps change dangerous habits without alienating traditional birth attendants. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T8#GNS313_U2_T8_h8)

question: Which of these makes an infection show up much faster (shortens the incubation period)?

options.A: Strong baseline immunity in the host
options.B: Slow replication rate of the pathogen
options.C: A very high initial infectious dose
options.D: Superficial entry through intact skin

explanation: Correct! If a huge number of germs enter your body at once, they don't need as much time to multiply before making you sick. [learn more](GNS313_U1_T9#GNS313_U1_T9_h3)

question: What kind of food is best to suggest for a patient suffering from painful mouth ulcers?

options.A: Hot, spicy, and crunchy snacks
options.B: Dry, salty crackers and toast
options.C: Acidic citrus fruits and juices
options.D: Cool, bland, and soft foods

explanation: Cool, soft, and gentle foods help keep the patient comfortable and avoid irritating sensitive sores. [learn more](GNS213_U3_T4#GNS213_U3_T4_h7)

question: What is the very first practical step when doing medication reconciliation during a home visit?

options.A: Calling the local pharmacy to order a fresh supply of all tablets
options.B: Gathering all current medication bottles and packages into one place
options.C: Asking the doctor to rewrite every prescription from the beginning
options.D: Throwing away any medicine that does not have a readable label

explanation: You got it! You have to round up all the medications first so you can actually see what the patient has and is taking. [learn more](GNS324_U3_T6#GNS324_U3_T6_h5)

question: Which method is commonly used to find out about past exposures in a case-control study?

options.A: Surgical intervention
options.B: Randomized clinical trials
options.C: Direct laboratory observation of future events
options.D: Interviews and questionnaires

explanation: Spot on! Since we are looking backward, we rely heavily on talking to patients and reviewing their past records using questionnaires and interviews. [learn more](GST114_U2_T19#GST114_U2_T19_h3)

question: Which of these is a classic example of a primary literature source?

options.A: A dictionary definition of the medical term hypertension
options.B: A systematic review article analyzing the findings of fifty different research papers
options.C: A nursing pharmacology textbook chapter listing common drug side effects
options.D: A research report detailing the exact methods and statistical results of a clinical trial

explanation: You nailed it. A direct research report with its own methods and data is always a primary source. [learn more](GNS217_U3_T6#GNS217_U3_T6_h2)

question: A patient tells you she uses petroleum jelly as a lubricant with her latex condoms. What should be your immediate nursing advice?

options.A: Confirm that petroleum jelly is the ideal choice for extra slip
options.B: Warn her that oil-based lubricants weaken latex and can cause breakage
options.C: Advise her to microwave the jelly first to make it safe for use
options.D: Suggest she switch to oil-based spermicide creams instead

explanation: Brilliant! Oil-based products break down latex rubber super fast, leading to tears. Water-based lube is always the safe choice here! [learn more](GNS226_U6_T016#GNS226_U6_T016_h6)

question: Why must a researcher conduct a literature review early in the process?

options.A: To decide which nurses will be punished for mistakes
options.B: To see what is already known and avoid repeating past work
options.C: To find patients willing to participate in the study
options.D: To determine the exact financial cost of the hospital

explanation: Reading prior studies prevents wasting time on questions that have already been answered thoroughly. [learn more](GNS217_U3_T1#GNS217_U3_T1_h2)

question: When is it safe for the transport nurse to leave the patient at the receiving hospital?

options.A: As soon as the wheels of the ambulance touch the hospital driveway
options.B: After the hospital staff officially assume full responsibility for care
options.C: The moment the stretcher is unlocked from the back of the vehicle
options.D: After calling the patient's family members on a mobile phone

explanation: Care must be continuous; leaving before a formal face-to-face handover leaves a dangerous gap in patient supervision. [learn more](GNS315_U3_T9#GNS315_U3_T9_h7)

question: Why are single-dose deworming treatments not enough on their own without better sanitation?

options.A: Environmental heat instantly neutralizes the therapeutic effect of drugs
options.B: Medicines only kill female worms and leave male worms untouched
options.C: Patients are quickly reinfected from contaminated soil and water sources
options.D: Adult worms immediately mutate to become immune to all known drugs

explanation: Medications clear out the worms you have, but without clean water and toilets, people just pick up new parasites from their surroundings right away. [learn more](GST114_U3_T6#GST114_U3_T6_h9)

question: What chemical alarm is released by damaged tissues to make blood vessels open up during inflammation?

options.A: Histamine
options.B: Insulin
options.C: Hemoglobin
options.D: Bilirubin

explanation: Well done! When cells get hurt, they release histamine. This chemical sounds the alarm, making blood vessels wider so white blood cells can rush easily to the rescue. [learn more](GNS123_U4_T2#GNS123_U4_T2_h3)

question: What is the main purpose of advance care planning?

options.A: To document a patient's treatment preferences before they lose capacity
options.B: To determine which medications are covered by insurance
options.C: To calculate the total financial cost of hospital treatment
options.D: To schedule nursing shifts for the upcoming week

explanation: Advance care planning lets people make their medical wishes known while they are still able to, ensuring their voice is respected even if they get too sick to speak later. [learn more](GNS321_U3_T5#GNS321_U3_T5_h9)

question: Why does the crossed extensor reflex happen at the same time as the withdrawal reflex?

options.A: To support body weight on the opposite limb when one limb is pulled away
options.B: To double the speed at which you pull your injured foot away from harm
options.C: To send an urgent pain signal directly up to the cerebral cortex for analysis
options.D: To make sure both legs move in the exact same direction at the same time

explanation: If you step on something sharp with your left foot, you lift it up. Your right leg automatically stiffens to hold your weight so you don't fall over! [learn more](GNS211_U3_T27#GNS211_U3_T27_h4)

question: What antibodies are found in the plasma of a person with Type AB blood?

options.A: Both anti-A and anti-B antibodies
options.B: Only anti-B antibodies
options.C: Neither anti-A nor anti-B antibodies
options.D: Only anti-A antibodies

explanation: Type AB blood has both A and B antigens on the cells, so the body does not make antibodies against either one, or it would attack its own blood. [learn more](GNS111_U2_T2#GNS111_U2_T2_h2)

question: Why are private discussions during home visits particularly beneficial for women's health assessments?

options.A: They prevent family members from ever asking questions about medications.
options.B: They legally replace the need for any laboratory blood testing.
options.C: They help women feel comfortable discussing sensitive issues like domestic safety.
options.D: They ensure the patient will never experience chronic illness.

explanation: Privacy builds confidence, allowing patients to safely share private health concerns, mental struggles, or safety risks at home. [learn more](GNS324_U3_T13#GNS324_U3_T13_h7)

question: When is the best time to talk about advance directives with a patient diagnosed with a brain degenerative disease?

options.A: Family members should make all choices without consulting the patient
options.B: After the patient has completely lost the ability to speak or think
options.C: Early in the disease process while the patient can still make decisions
options.D: During an emergency room visit in the final week of life

explanation: Makes total sense! Talking early ensures the patient's own values guide their future care before cognitive decline takes away their voice. [learn more](GNS222_U4_T13#GNS222_U4_T13_h7)

question: How does a newborn baby naturally receive passive immunity from their mother?

options.A: Through breast milk and across the placenta
options.B: By developing mild infections in the nursery
options.C: By receiving routine infant vaccinations at birth
options.D: Through exposure to sunlight during infancy

explanation: You nailed it! Mums pass helpful antibodies to their babies across the placenta during pregnancy and through breast milk after birth. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T83#GNS214_U1_T83_h4)

question: After a very tough loss on the children's ward, what best helps the nursing team cope with the stress?

options.A: Forcing the team to take on extra admissions to stay busy
options.B: Pretending the event did not happen to maintain normal routines
options.C: Punishing the nurses immediately for failing to save the patient
options.D: Providing a safe space for structured team debriefing and counseling

explanation: Talking through grief together in a supportive session helps nurses heal and prevents long-term emotional burnout. [learn more](GST321_U3_T7#GST321_U3_T7_h6)

question: How does community critical care connect to wider public health goals?

options.A: By tracking disease outbreaks, educating the public, and promoting early recognition of danger signs
options.B: By replacing all national public health vaccination programs
options.C: By focusing exclusively on treating isolated patients inside locked clinic rooms
options.D: By restricting health education to urban teaching hospitals only

explanation: Community nursing goes beyond the clinic doors by keeping an eye out for outbreaks and teaching families how to spot danger early. [learn more](GNS321_U2_T13#GNS321_U2_T13_h8)

question: A home care nurse is helping a diabetic patient manage blood sugar using local Nigerian foods. What is the best approach?

options.A: Insist the patient only eat imported foods recommended in standard textbooks
options.B: Tell the patient to stop eating altogether until blood sugar normalizes
options.C: Ignore the diabetes and let the patient eat whatever they want
options.D: Adapt the diabetic meal plan using accessible local staples and traditional foods

explanation: Brilliant! Good nursing means working with familiar, local foods so the patient can easily stick to their health plan. [learn more](GNS324_U3_T7#GNS324_U3_T7_h3)

question: What is a clear sign that an expectorant is working successfully?

options.A: The cough becomes more productive and brings up phlegm easily
options.B: The patient develops a high fever and chills overnight
options.C: The cough stops completely within ten minutes of the first dose
options.D: The lung sounds change from clear to heavy coarse crackles

explanation: You got it! Success means the patient can finally clear out that gunk easily instead of having a tight, dry, miserable chest. [learn more](GNS223_U2_T3#GNS223_U2_T3_h7)

question: Why is the rise of non-communicable diseases changing the daily work of primary health care nurses?

options.A: It completely eliminates the need for basic medications in rural clinics
options.B: It means nurses no longer need to worry about immunizing infants against infections
options.C: It allows nurses to stop providing care and refer every patient immediately abroad
options.D: It requires long-term patient education, lifestyle coaching, and chronic disease monitoring

explanation: Chronic conditions like diabetes and hypertension demand ongoing support, lifestyle guidance, and continuous follow-up from nurses. [learn more](GNS124_U1_T2#GNS124_U1_T2_h7)

question: When writing a good research question, which of these is an absolute must?

options.A: It must guarantee positive results for the hospital
options.B: It must be broad enough to change every nursing policy at once
options.C: It must use complex Latin terms to sound professional
options.D: It must be feasible to answer with available time and resources

explanation: Keep it realistic! Feasible simply means you have the time, money, and access to patients to actually finish the study without stressing out. [learn more](GNS217_U3_T8#GNS217_U3_T8_h2)

question: What is the general rule for how women with vulval varicose veins give birth?

options.A: A scheduled caesarean section is required in every single case
options.B: Labor must be induced early at thirty-six weeks gestation
options.C: Vaginal delivery is usually safe and successful for most women
options.D: Forceps delivery must be used to protect the perineal blood vessels

explanation: Good news! Having vulval varicosities doesn't automatically mean a C-section. Most mothers have safe, normal vaginal deliveries with proper supportive care. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T9#GNS216_U5_T9_h6)

question: Why do we consider pregnant teenagers and malnourished children as high-risk groups?

options.A: They have finished all required community health immunization schedules
options.B: They face a higher probability of poor health outcomes due to biological and social factors
options.C: They always live in urban hospital settings with easy access to doctors
options.D: They consume more public health resources than any other age group

question: What is the medical term for the one-sided lower belly pain some women feel during ovulation?

question: Which process completely destroys ALL microbial life, including tough spores?

question: Why should you tell a patient that a steroid nasal spray won't clear a stuffy nose instantly like a decongestant spray?

question: Why is homeostasis called a dynamic state instead of just staying completely still?

options.D: Extracellular fluid constantly changes into intracellular fluid to provide energy

question: What must a birth attendant do if a sterile item from the kit accidentally falls onto the floor?

question: Why do we prefer feeding through a stomach tube rather than an IV drip when the patient's digestive system is working?

question: Why do the cells in our body constantly need blood flowing to them?

question: Up to how many days after childbirth can a mother's death still be classified as maternal mortality?

question: How does qualitative data analysis differ from quantitative analysis?

question: Which of the following best describes the multi-faceted role of a nurse working in a Nigerian primary health center?

question: What is the main sign that a mum is experiencing distress during labour?

question: How do sperm mostly travel upward through the female reproductive tract?

question: A nurse accidentally pricks a finger with a used needle of unknown status. What is the very first thing to do?

question: A new mother complains that her left calf is severely painful, swollen, and warm to the touch. What should you suspect first?

options.D: Mastitis

question: How does close communication between nurses and family caregivers impact client care?

question: What is the best nursing action for a patient who cannot safely swallow food by mouth?

question: What is a vital legal and clinical truth Nigerian nurses must know about post-abortion care?

question: What is the main purpose of using a syringe driver in clinical practice?

question: What is the primary setting targeted by the School Health Programme?

question: Why must you turn an unconscious patient onto their side before cleaning their mouth?

question: A patient has a stubborn rash that won't go away with standard treatment, so a skin biopsy is ordered. What is the goal?

question: Which test is mainly used to check electrical brain waves and diagnose seizures?

question: How do vaccines protect the human body against specific diseases?

question: Why do community nutrition programs sometimes struggle when they introduce unfamiliar foreign foods?

question: Why must observations be independent when doing a Chi-Square test?

question: What is the main benefit of involving local stakeholders in a community health project?

question: How do membrane filters clean liquid solutions of microorganisms?

question: Why are people with long-term leg swelling at higher risk for skin infections like cellulitis?

question: What is the main goal of leadership theories in nursing?

question: What is the main goal of nursing care for a patient at the end of life?

question: Why is it so tricky to diagnose Lassa fever early just by looking at symptoms?

question: What is a key duty of a nurse acting as a facilitator in a community?

question: What is a major long-term risk of persistent, chronic inflammation in the body?

question: Why must patients finish every single dose of their prescribed antibiotics for a bacterial STI?

question: What happens when a manager tries to set too many objectives at the same time?

question: Which physical sign indicates that a patient is experiencing severe respiratory distress before treatment?

question: What is the best first step for a unit manager when an unexpected error happens on the ward?

question: When is a nurse most likely to consider using the rectal route for a patient?

question: What does 'Unity of Command' mean for teams working in an emergency center?

question: Why is tracking near-expiry drugs important for protecting a DRF?

question: Which of the following is a well-known long-term reproductive complication of untreated salpingitis?

question: Why are omega-3 fatty acids particularly important in the diet of a breastfeeding mother?

question: What stops large blood proteins and red blood cells from entering the filtrate in a healthy kidney?

question: In inventory management, what does the acronym FEFO stand for?

question: During birth, the baby's chin tucks tightly against its chest. What is this movement called?

question: What is the primary tool midwives use to track the progress of labour on a chart?

question: You want to find out which months malaria cases peak and food is scarcest in a farming village. Which tool should you use?

options.B: A structural house blueprint

question: You walk past some open gutters filled with stagnant water near residential houses. What major health risk does this environment create?

question: What is the primary medication class used as first-line treatment for minimal change disease?

options.A: Antivirals

question: Why is keeping a detailed maintenance log for cold chain equipment important?

options.D: It replaces the need to check temperatures twice daily

question: Why does the pulse oximeter algorithm focus specifically on pulsating arterial blood?

options.A: To calculate the exact speed of blood flow through the heart valves

options.C: To measure the total volume of red blood cells in the bone marrow

question: Which of these is NOT a common barrier to getting contraceptives in Nigeria?

options.C: Judgmental attitudes from healthcare workers
options.D: Universal availability of free home-delivery services

question: A typhoid patient suddenly complains of severe, sharp belly pain and their tummy feels hard to the touch. What emergency does this point to?

options.C: Pulmonary embolism
options.D: Splenic rupture

explanation: Correct! A rigid tummy and sudden sharp pain are red flags for a perforated bowel—this needs urgent surgical help right away. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T17#GNS313_U2_T17_h6)

question: Why do communicable diseases spread so quickly in crowded IDP camps?

options.A: Close living quarters and poor sanitation facilities
options.B: Frequent distribution of expired food supplies

options.D: Mandatory daily group physical exercise routines

question: Which of these is a clear example of an unsafe injection habit?

options.C: Dropping a used syringe straight into a safety box

question: What do we call the breathing difficulty that gets worse when a patient lies flat?

options.B: Inability to speak full sentences due to pain
options.C: Breathlessness that worsens when lying flat
options.D: Shortness of breath triggered by cold air

question: What is the main use of an action plan when implementing a program?

options.A: Calculating the total profit generated by the health facility

options.C: Breaking high-level goals down into specific daily and weekly tasks
options.D: Punishing staff members who fail to meet unrealistic deadlines

explanation: An action plan takes big, scary project goals and chops them into bite-sized daily and weekly steps that are easy to manage. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T20#GNS225_U2_T20_h4)

question: What is the primary purpose of using a surgical safety checklist in the labor ward?

options.A: To slow down emergency cesarean sections unnecessarily
options.B: To give doctors extra paperwork to fill out after work
options.C: To make sure vital safety steps are never skipped during care
options.D: To replace the need for professional nursing judgment

explanation: Checklists act as a memory aid to ensure critical safety checks are completed before, during, and after procedures. [learn more](GNS312_U5_T3#GNS312_U5_T3_h5)

question: Why do doctors frequently order a chest CT scan for a patient diagnosed with osteosarcoma?

options.A: To screen for concurrent rib fractures

options.C: To check for early metastasis to the lungs
options.D: To evaluate heart function before surgery

question: Why do clinics use more than one test (an algorithm) instead of just one rapid test for a positive result?

question: What is a common challenge in hospitals when national economic resources are limited?

options.A: Excessive hospital bed space in rural communities

options.D: Too many operational intensive care units

question: Why is a patient told to take a deep breath and hold it while a chest or surgical drain is being removed?

options.B: It completely stops the patient from feeling any discomfort at all
options.C: It relaxes the abdominal muscles so the stitches fall apart

explanation: Holding the breath creates a little bit of internal pressure, stopping air from being sucked into the empty tract as the tube comes out. [learn more](GNS212_U1_T22#GNS212_U1_T22_h7)

question: Why are nurses in a great position to act as health educators?

question: What should you do if an old gauze dressing is stuck tightly to a healing wound?

options.A: Leave the old gauze stuck and put new dressings on top.

options.C: Soak the whole patient in hot soapy water.

question: Which Nigerian agency leads national disease tracking and outbreak responses?

question: What is the most important first step when treating a baby with acute diarrhea?

options.D: Stopping all forms of breastfeeding immediately

question: Why must flight nurses be great at making quick, independent decisions?

question: What does a mixed methods research study combine?

question: How does a poorly designed hospital ward directly affect you as a nurse?

options.C: It guarantees higher salaries for working in difficult spaces

question: Which finding in a new mother's lochia (postnatal discharge) should worry you the most?

question: Why is cyanosis considered a poor early indicator of hypoxia?

question: Why do nurse managers use bar charts instead of long tables of numbers?

question: A nurse cares for an immobile surgery patient who is showing poor wound healing and muscle wasting. What is the most likely cause?

question: Which clotting protein increases a lot during pregnancy to prepare for childbirth?

question: A home care nurse gets stuck in terrible traffic and flooded roads on the way to a patient. What is the immediate effect of this delay?

question: A patient whispers to you in panic that she used a dangerous herbal mix to try and stop her pregnancy. How should you respond?

question: Why is the nursing history an essential part of a comprehensive assessment?

question: What is the big difference in how our bodies handle bacterial STIs compared to viral STIs?

question: What is one key reason for conducting a community diagnosis?

question: A community refuses to bring sick relatives to the clinic because of rumors that nurses cause infections. How should you respond?

question: How do tumbu fly larvae usually find their way into the human body?

question: Why must nurses gently correct unverified medication myths with pregnant patients?

question: What does noticeable muscle wasting in the temples and shoulders suggest about a patient?

question: How can a nurse help ensure a patient on a soft diet gets enough nutrition?

question: Which healthcare professional helps recovering accident victims relearn everyday tasks like dressing, bathing, and eating?

options.C: It lowers the total cost of hospital admission for surgical patients
options.D: It helps medical teams choose the right antibiotic treatment quickly

explanation: You've got this! Growing and identifying the exact germ helps the medical team target the infection with the exact right medicine. [learn more](GST114_U5_T4#GST114_U5_T4_h1)

question: What must you always check regarding traction weights during patient care?

options.A: Ensure they hang freely without touching the floor
options.B: Remove them every hour to let the muscles rest
options.C: Increase the weight if the patient complains of pain
options.D: Rest them on a stool when turning the patient

explanation: Weights must hang completely free! If they touch the floor or bed, the pulling force stops working. Simple check, big impact. [learn more](GNS221_U1_T8#GNS221_U1_T8_h4)

question: Which everyday habit causes a person to swallow extra air?

options.A: Sleeping on the left side
options.B: Chewing gum
options.C: Eating green leafy vegetables
options.D: Drinking plain water slowly

explanation: Chewing gum makes you swallow air without realizing it, which adds to the gas buildup in your tummy. Good to know for patient teaching! [learn more](GNS212_U1_T10#GNS212_U1_T10_h3)

question: Why is prioritization necessary after collecting community health data?

options.A: Government regulations forbid treating more than one disease at a time
options.B: Minor health issues are completely unimportant and should be ignored forever
options.C: It helps nurses avoid doing any field work for the rest of the year
options.D: Resources like time and money are limited, so the most urgent issues must be tackled first

explanation: Because resources are finite, prioritization ensures the most pressing and impactful health problems receive attention first. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T17#GNS225_U2_T17_h6)

question: Why is communication evaluated right alongside clinical nursing skills?

options.A: Soft skills replace the need for formal nursing board examinations
options.B: Clinical skills are entirely separate from how a nurse talks to patients
options.C: Communication scores are the only data required by insurance companies
options.D: Nursing requires effective teamwork and clear handovers to keep patients safe

explanation: Even if you are great at procedures, nursing is a team sport. Clear handovers and warm patient communication are vital to prevent mistakes. [learn more](GST321_U1_T21#GST321_U1_T21_h2)

question: In conservative communities, how is family honor often tied to female family members?

options.A: Through their ability to generate personal business wealth
options.B: Through their athletic achievements in school
options.C: Through their election into local political office
options.D: Through their perceived sexual purity and chastity

explanation: That's right. Traditional communities unfortunately place the heavy burden of family reputation squarely on the sexual purity and behavior of women and girls. [learn more](GNS312_U1_T12#GNS312_U1_T12_h5)

question: Which of these is NOT something a nurse should do when dealing with harmful traditional practices?

options.A: Performing the harmful traditional practice to please community elders
options.B: Offering supportive counseling to women resisting the practice
options.C: Providing respectful health education on the dangers involved
options.D: Reporting illegal procedures or child abuse to the right authorities

explanation: As a nurse, your first loyalty is to your patient's safety. You should never take part in harmful traditional practices, no matter the local pressure! [learn more](GNS216_U1_T8#GNS216_U1_T8_h8)

question: Why do some topical medications bypass first-pass liver metabolism?

options.A: They are formulated to only stay in the top layer of skin cells
options.B: They enter the body without travelling through the digestive tract first
options.C: They require liver enzymes to activate their chemical structure
options.D: They are completely destroyed by skin enzymes before absorption

explanation: Because topical drugs are absorbed through the skin or mucous membranes rather than swallowed, they avoid the portal vein system that leads to early liver metabolism. [learn more](GNS125_U3_T16#GNS125_U3_T16_h1)

question: What is the most crucial nursing action when caring for a patient having a severe endocrine emergency like a thyroid storm?

options.A: Closely monitoring vital signs and supporting stable organ function
options.B: Withholding prescribed medications until lab results return
options.C: Restricting all fluid intake to prevent swelling and weight gain
options.D: Encouraging heavy physical exercise to burn off excess energy

explanation: Endocrine emergencies cause wild, dangerous shifts in vitals and metabolism. Keeping a close eye on vital signs and giving steady supportive care is always your top priority. [learn more](GNS222_U2_T13#GNS222_U2_T13_h8)

question: What is the very first step in the process of urine formation?

options.A: Tubular reabsorption
options.B: Water concentration
options.C: Tubular secretion
options.D: Glomerular filtration

explanation: Filtration occurs first in the renal corpuscle, forcing fluid and small solutes out of the blood and into Bowman's capsule. [learn more](GNS121_U2_T1#GNS121_U2_T1_h4)

question: A nurse notices that a patient's skin is very dry and lacks normal turgor. Which physiological issue does this most likely suggest?

options.A: Dehydration and fluid volume deficit
options.B: Excessive vitamin D production
options.C: Normal localized blood pooling
options.D: High levels of subcutaneous fat

explanation: Poor skin turgor and dryness are classic clinical signs of fluid loss and dehydration. [learn more](GNS211_U2_T5#GNS211_U2_T5_h8)

question: When is the best time to introduce palliative care to a cancer patient?

options.A: Early alongside active disease treatment to improve quality of life
options.B: Only when the patient refuses to take prescribed oral medications
options.C: Only during the final twenty-four hours of life
options.D: After all chemotherapy and radiation treatments have failed completely

explanation: Palliative care isn't just for the end of life—it teams up with curative treatments from day one to keep the patient comfortable. Excellent holistic nursing! [learn more](GNS321_U1_T10#GNS321_U1_T10_h8)

question: What is a major danger of misusing drugs in healthcare settings?

options.A: Immediate reduction in the overall cost of running hospitals
options.B: Development of antimicrobial resistance to common infections
options.C: Faster recovery times for patients with chronic illnesses
options.D: Decreased workload for nurses on the hospital wards

explanation: When we overuse antibiotics, germs learn how to fight back and survive, making common infections much harder to treat later. [learn more](GNS215_U1_T5#GNS215_U1_T5_h4)

question: What is the best initial position for a patient experiencing acute respiratory distress?

options.A: High Fowler's position
options.B: Flat on the back
options.C: Trendelenburg position
options.D: Left lateral recovery position

explanation: Sitting upright in high Fowler's position allows gravity to lower the diaphragm, giving the lungs maximum room to expand and making breathing easier. [learn more](GNS213_U2_T11#GNS213_U2_T11_h5)
